name: Noel case and Herrick’s 1910 report
description: James Herrick’s 1910 report described unusual red blood cell shapes in Walter Clement Noel, a student from Grenada.

impact.note: One case report, the first description of sickle cells, known mainly to physicians and followed by later case studies, with the larger research line credited to later work.

date.basis: The date is scoped to this described observation, text, archaeological interpretation or object, not the origin of the wider practice.

events.statement: James Herrick’s 1910 report described unusual red blood cell shapes in Walter Clement Noel, a student from Grenada.

evidence.supports: The selected reproduction of Herrick’s 1910 paper reports unusual red-cell morphology in an anaemic patient and explicitly states that a definite diagnosis could not be made. It is an excerpt reprinted in 2014, not the full five-page original report.

The NHLBI historical timeline identifies Walter Clement Noel, a student from Grenada, as the patient described by Herrick in 1910. The report does not mean his was the first occurrence or prior community knowledge of the disease.

events.caveats: The cited 2014 reproduction contains selected excerpts, not the full original paper. Herrick explicitly said a definite diagnosis could not be made; later disease classification and community knowledge should not be projected back into this case.
